pairs.subject: admission-queue
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/worker.rs:614 The per-run timing clock starts when the job is claimed, so the run's durable JobStages record (run/index/hooks/alerts/total, where total is 'Claim → end of fan-out') never stores how long the job waited in the queue; a fast executor behind a slow queue looks like a slow executor. Two more deviations: the worker promotes on slot count with no host-pressure gate, and the refresher's skipped probes are never counted.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/worker.rs:614 StageWatch is seeded from the claim instant. Queue wait (available_at → claim) is not recorded as its own measurement on the run. created_at is the wrong 'arrived' instant for scheduled jobs because available_at gates them. Core does expose oldest_queued_secs, but no per-run wait split exists.

crates/server/src/worker.rs:44 Promotion is gated only by the global semaphore and per-app caps. No host signal (memory/CPU) is checked before claiming, and a search of server/core for sysinfo/loadavg/pressure/high_water found no pressure gate.

crates/server/src/refresher.rs:122 Probe-and-skip is done right: a non-blocking idle-slot probe, the skip ends the submission, and a later demand fetch takes over. But a skip just runs `continue` with no counter or metric (only `refreshed` is logged, at debug), so the technique's 'count the skips separately' rule is unmet.

crates/server/src/refresher.rs:106 The refresher runs on the scheduler's own clock with a per-drain cap (global_per_tick plus per_host_per_tick) and an overlap guard. The worker waking per enqueue falls under the per-item-execution exemption.

crates/server/src/fanout.rs:26 The line count is a stated decision: separate fan-out and delivery pools because their backpressure means different things. The job queue is one line in front of a pool of identical workers, and per-app blocked lists stop a capped app from blocking the head of the line.

crates/server/src/fanout.rs:64 The fan-out backlog is bounded (fanout_max_queued) with a named shed policy (run inline, never drop), extracted and tested. Caveat: placement() reads inflight and fetch_add (line 137) takes the slot separately, so concurrent callers can overshoot the bound by up to the number of simultaneous arrivals.

crates/server/src/worker.rs:43 Priority ordering with configurable aging (the claim_next ORDER BY uses priority plus age divided by the coefficient), plus per-app occupancy caps from blocked_apps/app_limit so one app cannot take every slot.

crates/server/src/worker.rs:252 Claiming stops when shutdown is signalled. Running jobs get a deadline-bounded clean finish, then a checkpoint suspend that re-queues them (park), then a recover_stuck sweep tagged with the drain reason. The fan-out and delivery pools are drained, and stragglers are counted and logged. Queued jobs stay durable in SQLite.
